title: Runtime & Control Plane Migration: compatibility and rollback playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working playbook for upgrading private deployments (VPC and on-prem) where we need coordinated changes across: the serving runtime, the private control plane, API surface compatibility, and Terraform modules. It prioritizes safe rollouts, automated validation, and clear rollback paths.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to private deployments running Redwood control plane v1.8.x or v1.9.x and serving runtime v2.0.x. Target upgrade path is control-plane v2.0.x + runtime v2.1.x.
- Terraform is used to manage infra + control plane resources with our terraform-modules repo. Existing customers may be on a forked module; this playbook covers both upstream module changes and local overrides.
- Network topologies covered: VPC-hosted private control plane (cloud-managed) and fully on-prem air-gapped installs.
- Key safety principle: runtime binary and control plane changes must be staged and validated independently before global traffic migration.

High-level strategy:
1) Pre-upgrade validation (dry-run): inventory, compatibility matrix, smoke tests against a staging cluster that mirrors production.
2) Terraform module rollout: introduce backward-compatible module changes (feature flags, new optional vars) and tested migration steps for state.
3) Canary control plane upgrade: upgrade a single tenant/control-plane replica or region, validate admin APIs, RBAC and certificate rotation.
4) Canary serving runtime upgrade: deploy runtime v2.1.x to a subset of nodes and route a small percentage of traffic using traffic-split.
5) Progressive traffic migration in waves, with rollback gates after each wave.
6) Post-upgrade verification and cleanup: remove compatibility shims and deprecated flags in subsequent minor releases.

Compatibility matrix (quick reference):
- control-plane v1.8/1.9 -> v2.0: introduces new /v2/admin endpoints; /v1 endpoints kept for read-only for 6 weeks.
- runtime v2.0 -> v2.1: supports new kv-cache on-disk format (opt-in). When the on-disk format is enabled, older runtimes cannot read caches.
- API contract: model-serving API (predict endpoints) remains backwards compatible; webhook payload schema adds optional fields (safe).
- Terraform modules: new outputs introduced (control_plane_certificate_id). Existing automation should not depend on the order of resources.

Pre-upgrade checklist (must be completed before starting):
- Create an upgrade ticket and slack channel, tag oncall, infra, and security. (JIRA: JIRA-INF-987)
- Snapshot Terraform state and store encrypted copy in customer vault.
- Backup cluster etcd (on-prem) or snapshot control-plane DB for cloud (if applicable).
- Validate current metrics and SLO baseline (30d baseline). Export dashboards and record pre-upgrade token latency, error rate, and tail p99.
- Validate rollback playbooks exist and are tested in staging.
- Confirm maintenance/upgrade window and customer notification if required.
- Verify KMS/HSM integration plan if control plane key rotation is required.

Terraform module notes and migration plan:
- Principle: make changes additive and optional for at least one minor release. Use feature flags on modules (e.g., enable_new_controlplane_v2 -> default false).
- Variables to add: control_plane_version (string), control_plane_cert_id (optional), enable_kv_cache_on_disk (bool, default false).
- Outputs: control_plane_endpoint, control_plane_certificate_id.
- State migration: if we rename resources, include a move block in instructions. Example: terraform state mv module.cp.aws_lb.old module.cp.aws_lb.new
- Upgrade steps: 1) bump module reference in root module but keep enable_new_controlplane_v2=false; 2) run terraform plan and review changes (expect zero change); 3) enable boolean flag for a canary environment only, run apply; 4) validate; 5) ramp flag to remaining envs in waves.
- Recommended local-run commands: terraform init -upgrade; terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars -out=tfplan; terraform apply tfplan. Always maintain an encrypted plan artifact and upload to ticket.
- Rollback considerations: because resource replacement may cause downtime, ensure we do not replace DB-backed resources in first pass. For replacements that are unavoidable, do them in maintenance window with DB failover testing.

Control plane upgrade (detailed):
- Canary strategy: pick a non-critical tenant or a single region replica. For on-prem single-DC customers, canary will be a single control-plane pod.
- Steps: stop autoscaler (prevent autoscaling thrash) -> drain control-plane instance -> apply new control-plane image. Wait for health checks to pass.
- Post-start checks: admin endpoints respond; webhooks still deliver; leader election stable; audit logs intact.
- Certificates: if new control-plane requires certificate rotation, use offline rotation flow for air-gapped installs (see linked Confluence doc CONFLUENCE-1234). Ensure control-plane cert change is propagated to agents before routing traffic.

Serving runtime upgrade (detailed):
- Binary compatibility: runtime v2.1 introduces optional on-disk KV cache. Default behavior is in-memory only. Do not enable on-disk cache for canary unless explicitly testing it.
- Docker image tags: use immutable tags (sha256) for release builds. Deploy canary as: image: redwood/runtime@sha256:<sha>.
- Deployment order: 1) drain low-priority nodes; 2) cordon node; 3) rollout new daemonset/daemonless pods with node-affinity (canary nodes); 4) start health check and warm KV caches with a synthetic workload.
- Traffic routing: use service mesh or traffic-split to send 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 100% traffic waves. Hold at each wave for at least 2x p99 latency window or 30 minutes, whichever is larger.

API compatibility validation tests (smoke + regression):
- Smoke: send a canonical set of requests covering streaming, function-calls, structured-output, embeddings, and rerank. Validate tokens and latency.
- Regression harness: run our eval-suite against a snapshot of prompts and compare outputs (automated diff). Alert on >0.5% regression in quality metrics or any critical response-format change.
- Edge tests: large context tokens, KV cache warm/replay, partial responses, and injected errors (simulate downstream timeouts).

Rollback procedures (fast and safe):
- Fast rollback (control plane): restore prior control plane image by re-applying previous manifest and confirm old endpoints are healthy. If DB migrations applied during control-plane upgrade are irreversible, rollback may be partial; DO NOT rollback if irreversible schema migration has run unless DB restore is available.
- Fast rollback (runtime): use image swap to previous sha and ramp traffic back using traffic-split. Sequence: set traffic-split for canary -> swap image -> confirm canary health -> increase traffic-split to previous state.
- Terraform rollback: revert module changes using the stored plan artifact or previous commit, run terraform apply. If resources were replaced, follow resource-specific rollback steps (see resource notes).
- Emergency DB restore: pre-approved playbook must be available. This is the nuclear option and requires oncall plus DB-admin approval.

Validation queries and alerts (examples):
- PromQL to detect increased token latency: rate(redwood_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]) by (le) -> compare p99 to baseline.
- Error rate spike: increase in 5xx responses: increase(rate(redwood_request_errors_total[5m])) > 3x baseline triggers pause.
- Model cache miss ratio: redwood_kv_cache_miss_total / redwood_kv_cache_requests_total > 0.05 for >15m -> investigate cache config.

On-prem vs VPC differences and gotchas:
- Networking: on-prem customers may require manual firewall/nat configuration for control-plane callbacks. Verify port whitelists before cert rotation or new admin endpoints.
- Air-gapped: pre-stage container images in local registry. Terraform operations that rely on cloud providers must be run from a bastion with credentials and not from fully air-gapped environment. Document the image import workflow.
- HSM/KMS: key rotation flows differ. For HSM-backed installs, coordinate with security to ensure key policies permit transient signatures during rotation.

Post-upgrade cleanup and follow-ups:
- Remove backward-compatibility flags in next minor release once customers have been on the new platform for >=6 weeks.
- Bump module defaults to new behavior after 2 minor releases.
- Create a follow-up task to run full integration tests in CI against sample customer manifests.
- Update runbooks and customer-facing upgrade notes.

Open questions / risks (TODOs):
- Should we enable on-disk KV cache as opt-in or default for future minor? (open: perf tests pending by Applied ML)
- Impact of control-plane DB schema migration on active sessions: PR to runtime to gracefully handle new schema is in review (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/210).
- Terraform state drift detection cadence for long-lived private deployments: recommend weekly drift scan job.

Runbook snippets (quick commands):
- Snapshot terraform: GPG_ENCRYPTED_PLAN=$(mktemp)
  terraform plan -out=tfplan -var-file=secrets.tfvars && terraform show -json tfplan > plan.json && gpg --encrypt --recipient "ops@redwood.ai" plan.json && mv plan.json.gpg ${GPG_ENCRYPTED_PLAN}
- Apply canary terraform changes: terraform apply -var=enable_new_controlplane_v2=true -target=module.control_plane["canary"]
- Roll runtime image back: kubectl -n redwood set image deployment/runtime runtime=redwood/runtime@sha256:<old-sha>
- Verify admin health: curl -s -k https://CONTROL_PLANE/admin/health | jq .status

Notes to self / miscellaneous:
- Keep customer notification template ready; include expected SLO windows and rollback guarantee language.
- Coordinate with Solutions Eng to offer assisted upgrade for any customers with custom Terraform.
- This doc will be reviewed in the next eng-private-deployments sync; move to final after one successful staged upgrade.

Appendix: quick-version compatibility mapping (human readable)
- control-plane 1.8.x -> runtime 2.0.x: supported (no changes)
- control-plane 1.9.x -> runtime 2.1.x: partially supported; must disable on-disk cache
- control-plane 2.0.x -> runtime 2.1.x: supported; recommended
- If in doubt, run the compatibility-checker script included in the terraform-modules repo.

End of draft.
